title: Assessment of and Humanitarian Aid for Gaza Crisis
what_it_is: Assessment of and Humanitarian Aid for Gaza Crisis

sections.label: Gaza humanitarian crisis and ETAP
sections.summary: Asks about Government plans to alleviate the Gaza humanitarian crisis and how the conflict affects Singapore's Enhanced Technical Assistance Package to the Palestinian Authority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs (a) what are the plans of the Government to help alleviate the humanitarian crisis faced by civilians in Gaza impacted by the recent conflict in Israel and Gaza in the Palestinian Territories; and (b) how does the conflict impact Singapore's Enhanced Technical Assistance Package (ETAP) currently rendered to support the Palestinian Authority through capacity building of Palestinian officials and scholarships for Palestinian postgraduate students.

sections.label: Support for Singaporeans in Israel Gaza
sections.summary: Asks what support Singapore has given Singaporeans in Israel or Gaza and how often consular emergency plans for Israel and Palestine are updated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs (a) what support has been provided or is being provided by the Singapore Government to Singaporeans living or working in Israel or Gaza since the outbreak of the current Israel-Hamas conflict; (b) how often are the consular emergency plans for Israel, Palestine and other hotspots around the world updated; and (c) when was the last time the consular emergency plans for Israel and Palestine were updated.

sections.label: Ramallah office and Palestinian Authority support
sections.summary: Asks about steps to ensure safety of Singapore's representative office in Ramallah and continued engagement and support for the Palestinian Authority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs in light of the ongoing conflict in Gaza and Singapore's longstanding relationship with the Palestinian Authority (a) what are the steps taken to ensure the safety of Singapore's representative office in Ramallah; (b) how will Singapore continue to engage the Palestinian Authority and provide support through programmes such as the Singapore Cooperation Programme and the Enhanced Technical Assistance Package; and (c) whether such assistance should be placed on hold to focus instead on more pressing needs like humanitarian aid efforts.

sections.label: Ceasefire call and Singapore's harmony
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government will consider calling for a ceasefire in Gaza and plans to safeguard Singapore's peace and harmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs (a) whether the Government will consider calling for a ceasefire in Gaza; and (b) what conditions or situations must come to pass before such a call for a ceasefire becomes imminent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs what are the Government's plans to safeguard Singapore's peace and harmony should the situation in Gaza and Israel deteriorate further and for longer.

sections.label: Two-state solution diplomatic efforts
sections.summary: Asks how Singapore can play a role in renewing diplomatic efforts for a negotiated two-state solution consistent with UN Security Council resolutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs how can Singapore play a role in renewing diplomatic efforts to work on a negotiated two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict that is consistent with relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions.

sections.label: Answers deferred to Motion debate
sections.summary: Seeks permission to answer the Parliamentary Questions during the later debate on the Motion on the Israel-Hamas Conflict.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: As these queries relate to the same subject matter as the upcoming Motion on "Solidarity, Security and Peace – the Israel-Hamas Conflict", which would be debated later today, I would like to seek your permission, Sir, on behalf of all the respective Ministers to whom the Parliamentary Questions have been directed, to provide answers to the questions during the debate on the Motion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: As there is obviously a lot of overlap, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, together with the other Ministries, will provide a response to the queries on the Order Paper during the debate on the Motion, in order to address them completely and holistically.
